chunks.title: Landmark Precedents in Indian Civil Law
chunks.content: # Landmark Precedents in Indian Civil Law

chunks.title: Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co., (1995) 5 SCC 545
chunks.content:
### Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co., (1995) 5 SCC 545
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India
**Core Holding:** Settled the cardinal principles governing grant of interlocutory injunctions under CPC Order 39. The court must assess prima facie case, balance of convenience, and whether refusing injunction results in irreparable loss. Equitable relief is denied to parties with unclean hands.

chunks.title: Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v. Kartick Das, (1994) 4 SCC 225
chunks.content:
### Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v. Kartick Das, (1994) 4 SCC 225
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India
**Core Holding:** Laid down strict parameters for ex-parte ad-interim injunctions: they should be granted only in exceptional circumstances where delay would defeat justice, with notice to the opposing party being the general rule.

chunks.title: Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai, (2003) 6 SCC 675
chunks.content:
### Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai, (2003) 6 SCC 675
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India
**Core Holding:** Clarified the scope of supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution and Section 115 CPC revisions against interlocutory orders of civil courts.

chunks.title: Burden of Proof & Pleading Rules
chunks.content:
### Burden of Proof & Pleading Rules
1. **Burden on Plaintiff:** Plaintiff must prove their affirmative claims on a balance of probabilities (Section 101/102 Evidence Act / BSA §104).
2. **Strict Adherence to Pleadings (Order 6 Rule 2):** Parties cannot lead evidence on facts not pleaded in the Plaint or Written Statement.
3. **Execution of Decrees (Order 21):** Money decrees and recovery of possession executed through attachment, sale, or civil detention.

chunks.title: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC)
chunks.content:
### Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC)
- **Section 9:** Courts have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred.
- **Section 11 (Res Judicata):** No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been heard and finally decided by a Court of competent jurisdiction.
- **Order 39 Rules 1 & 2 (Temporary Injunctions):** Grounded on the tripartite test: (1) Prima facie case; (2) Balance of convenience; (3) Irreparable injury that cannot be adequately compensated in monetary damages.
- **Order 7 Rule 11 (Rejection of Plaint):** Plaint rejected where it does not disclose a cause of action, is barred by any law (e.g. Limitation Act), or is insufficiently stamped.

chunks.title: Specific Relief Act, 1963 (SRA)
chunks.content:
### Specific Relief Act, 1963 (SRA)
- **Section 10 (Specific Performance):** Specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to statutory exceptions, making specific enforcement mandatory rather than discretionary following the 2018 amendment.
- **Section 14 (Contracts Not Specifically Enforceable):** Contracts involving personal skills or continuous supervision cannot be specifically enforced.
- **Section 34 (Declaratory Decrees):** Court may make a declaration of legal character or right where plaintiff is entitled to any legal character or property right.
- **Section 38 (Perpetual Injunctions):** Granted to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in favor of the plaintiff.

chunks.title: Indian Limitation Act, 1963
chunks.content:
### Indian Limitation Act, 1963
- Suits for breach of contract, recovery of money, or specific performance have a general limitation period of 3 years from the date of cause of action.
